verdict.line: You lose when you eat a Rupture into a level-6 Feast all-in; you win nearly every poke war once your core items land.

brief.thesis: Cho'Gath's only real poke, Rupture, actually outranges your Shock Blast (950 vs 600) and is on a 9s cooldown, so this lane is a patience check: bait the Q, punish the long whiff window, and never let him land it into a Feral Scream or a level-6 Feast. The numbers back that up — 49.3% Jayce win rate over 205 games, with lane and solo-kill edge on your side once you play it right.

theirWindow.when: Right after Rupture lands on you
theirWindow.what: He'll walk in to stack Vorpal Spikes autos, and from level 6 on a low-HP target he can follow with Feast for a near-instant kill. Disengage immediately instead of trading through the knock-up.

yourWindow.what: He has no gap-close and Rupture is down for 9s — flip to Cannon Stance and punish with Shock Blast or Hyper Charge-empowered autos before he can reset to max range.

start.why: Run by 93% of Jayce players in this matchup (47.8% win rate, 226 games) — the extra sustain and early damage let you contest Vorpal Spikes trades before you have Lightning Field mana back.

boots.why: Posts a 55.2% win rate over 58 games here, and the Tenacity directly cuts the duration of Rupture's slow and Feral Scream's silence — the exact two tools that chain into his kill pressure.

runes.keystoneWhy: Best measured win rate on this matchup (50.9% over the top page) — the movement speed proc after landing two abilities is exactly what you need to close a Shock Blast poke into a dash-away before his next Rupture.

summoners.why: Flash+Teleport is the most common and highest-win-rate pairing here (51%, 56.6% pick) — Teleport resets you to lane after you abuse Youmuu's/Shock Blast to shove waves, and Flash covers Feast all-in angles. Flash+Ignite (44.4%) is the alt pick if you're confident in solo-killing him early.

playing.title: Bait Rupture, then poke
playing.detail: Hold max range in Cannon Stance so his Q (Rupture, 950 range, 9s cooldown) has to be thrown speculatively. The instant it misses, flip stance and punish with Shock Blast or empowered autos before it's back up.

playing.title: Never auto-trade into fresh spikes
playing.detail: E (Vorpal Spikes) procs on every one of his autos at point-blank range with a 0.5s cooldown — walking into melee to trade autos loses to this every time, especially pre-6.

playing.title: Respect Feral Scream from level 4 on
playing.detail: W (Feral Scream) is a 300-range cone that silences. Getting tagged mid-combo cancels your stance-swap rotation outright, so stay past 300 range whenever its 13s cooldown is up.

playing.title: Play around Feast at level 6
playing.detail: R (Feast) deals high true damage at 175 range and grows him on a kill (max 6 stacks). Don't sit below roughly 30% HP inside his melee range once he hits 6.

playing.title: Spike hard after Tear into Muramana
playing.detail: Once Muramana is online your Shock Blast poke scales sharply and Youmuu's active lets you disengage after every bait — this is your best all-in window of the game (levels 9-13).

playing.title: Clear waves from range, not melee
playing.detail: Use Cannon Stance Shock Blast to shove and clear from max range instead of auto-trading. This denies his Vorpal Spikes stacks and the health/mana he recovers from Carnivore on kills.

playing.title: Pick Mercury's Treads over Lucidity here
playing.detail: Tenacity shortens both Feral Scream's silence and Rupture's slow, which breaks the exact chain he needs to land a kill — take this whenever he's landing CC combos, not just for raw stats.

brief.patchCaveat: Build paths, rune pages, boots, summoners, and all win-rate/sample figures above are pulled directly from measured games on the current patch; the tactical reasoning connecting them to specific cooldowns and trade windows is my own read of the kits.
